quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means the driver will:
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended upward means the driver will turn right. Change your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you to watch for bicycles crossing.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: As safe as driving under normal conditions.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Focus on driving to prevent crashes.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Drive slower to reduce the risk.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can hurt your driving ability. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means the driver will:
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended downward means the driver will stop. Change your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: If traffic is backing up behind you because you are driving slowly, you should:

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you because you are driving slowly, pull off the road and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly when a tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel tightly to stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator and reduce speed. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes gently and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: You are driving uphill behind a heavy truck. Which statement is true?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. When visibility is limited on a hill, passing another vehicle is illegal. Be cautious when approaching large vehicles from behind.

questions.question: In a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. Report the crash to police if there are injuries, deaths, or property damage over $1,000 (or over $200 in damage to public property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires improve traction on icy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving requires extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. This helps you avoid hitting other vehicles.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. Sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: You see a "45 mph where workers present" sign. What should you do?

options.text: Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.
questions.explanation: In work zones with this sign, slow down only when workers are present. You can drive the normal speed limit when no workers are visible. Always watch for workers and reduce speed to protect them.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs about how many feet to stop?
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need much longer stopping distances than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph may need about 400 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: It starts raining while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when rain reduces visibility. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull off the road safely and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at this exact speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the highest legal speed you can drive on this road. In bad weather like rain, snow, or ice, you must drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Where should your car be after the turn?

options.text: In the center of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, end your turn in the lane closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: You are driving at night toward another car. What should your headlights be set to?
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another car is coming toward you or when you are following another car at night. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: How should you enter a highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Speed up to get ahead of other cars.
Drive slowly to avoid hitting other cars.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to traffic speed, and merge into the traffic safely.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and cars with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces that are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What is the main danger shown by this sign?

options.text: Your headlights may be misaligned because one side of your car is higher.
A tire could be damaged if you drift onto the shoulder.
Your car could hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You could lose control of your car if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control of your car if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your car.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to turn as cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, to the sides, and at the rear. Avoid these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: A car is entering the freeway from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert them.
Change lanes or slow down to give them space.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to give them space.
questions.explanation: Make room for cars entering the freeway. Change lanes if you can to let them merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them space.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You can concentrate better and feel calm.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can concentrate better and feel calm.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your eyesight, changes how you judge speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you and there is a right lane, move to it. If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when it is safe. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what is important to do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is empty before you enter it.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the other vehicles in the procession can follow through, even if the traffic light says they should not.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Can either continue through or exit from your lane.
Can stay in your lane and continue through.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane leaves the freeway on a ramp. You can change lanes to continue on the freeway, or you must exit.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before you go.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them as stop signs.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, the chance of a collision increases. If you drive faster than surrounding traffic, you will have to keep passing others. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When is it safe to use cruise control?

options.text: When driving in rural areas with light traffic.
When driving in heavy rain and snow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in rural areas with light traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic, near many exits and entrances, or on slippery roads from rain, snow, or ice. Constantly resetting cruise control can distract you and increase crash risk. Most manufacturers do not recommend cruise control when towing heavy loads.

questions.question: What happens when a driver goes much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: They are a very safe driver.
They should not let following cars pass.
They may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull off the road to let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side of the road with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as the traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side of the road with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they face the traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the aggressive driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get revenge escalates the situation and increases danger.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop immediately and block their path.
Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
Signal to tell them when it is clear to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, do everything possible to give them a clear path. If safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through.

questions.question: When two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: When you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle. You may then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: For which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way when turning left?
questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When the traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you cannot stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you cannot stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light approaching an intersection, slow down and stop before entering if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.
